title: add-transactional-downgrade-guard-backup-restore-version-pinning-private-installer
author: Sana Patel
commit_summary: a1f3b2c: add transactional schema migration runner and test harness
c4d5e6f: implement downgrade guard checks and version pinning in installer
d7e8f90: add backup/restore helpers and S3-compatible integration for on-prem
f1a2b3c: wire upgrade/rollback CLI commands and Helm hooks
b4c5d6e: docs: add upgrade/rollback runbook and API notes
description:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private need a safe, repeatable upgrade path that supports schema migrations, reliable backups, and guaranteed rollback (downgrade) guards. Previous upgrades were best-effort and occasionally led to incompatible state when a downgrade was required. This PR adds transactional schema migrations, explicit version pinning for critical components, backup/restore tooling for on-prem S3-compatible stores, and automated downgrade-guard checks integrated into the private-installer.

What this PR does:
- Transactional schema migrations: new migration runner (private-installer/migrations) that applies up/down migrations inside a single transaction where possible and records migration checksums. Works with Postgres and supports safe retries.
- Downgrade guard: installer now verifies target version compatibility and will refuse a downgrade unless a validated backup exists and the database schema is compatible. The guard hooks into Helm pre-upgrade/post-upgrade and the installer CLI.
- Version pinning: critical control-plane components (controller, api-server, auth-service) can be pinned via installer config; default pins are provided for release branches. Pins are validated during upgrade.
- Backup/restore: add backup operator and restore CLI using pluggable storage (S3-compatible). Backups are consistent with migration checkpoints and include schema and application state snapshots.
- Rollback tooling: CLI and Helm hooks to perform safe rollback using the latest validated backup; includes automated post-rollback integrity checks.

Checklist:
- [x] Migration runner implemented and unit tested
- [x] Downgrade guard + validation integrated into installer
- [x] Backup/restore implemented and e2e-tested with local MinIO
- [x] CLI commands (upgrade/rollback/backup/restore) documented
- [x] Release notes and runbook added

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for migration runner and downgrade guard (CI)
- E2E upgrade->backup->rollback scenario using MinIO in CI (script: scripts/ci/e2e-upgrade.sh)
- Manual testing against a staging VPC deployment with a seeded dataset showing deterministic rollback path

Backward compatibility and safety:
- Default behavior is opt-in for pinning; existing installs are not forced to pin unless the operator enables it.
- Downgrade guard can be overridden with explicit operator acknowledgement (safeguarded) but requires a validated backup to proceed.
- Migrations record checksums to prevent partial-applies on downgrade.

Linear/Jira: ENG-4321 (migrations), ENG-4390 (backup/restore), SUP-980 (support follow-up).

Notes for reviewers: focus review on the migration transaction boundaries (private-installer/migrations/runner.go), the downgrade guard validation logic (installer/rollback/guard.go), and the backup format (installer/backup/format.md). The Helm hooks are intentionally minimal; we prefer guard logic in the installer binary rather than complex Helm lifecycle scripting.
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Can you confirm that migrations are idempotent and safe to retry? Please add a comment in runner.go explaining the retry semantics.
Sana Patel: Added explanation and added unit test for retry path. Ran e2e to validate idempotency against Postgres 13 and 14.
Anika Bose: Backup format looks good. Question: do we encrypt backups by default for on-prem S3?
Sana Patel: Backups default to server-side encryption when supported by the target store; added config and docs to explain toggles.
Ethan Liu: The downgrade guard refusal message should include remediation steps (how to create/validate backup). Please include CLI hints.
Sana Patel: Updated CLI help and runbook with explicit commands to snapshot/validate/restore; included example commands in docs/private-installer/upgrade-rollback.md
release_notes:
- Added transactional schema migration runner to private-installer
- Introduced downgrade guard to prevent unsafe rollbacks (requires validated backup)
- Backup/restore tooling for S3-compatible stores (MinIO tested)
- CLI commands: redwood-installer upgrade|rollback|backup|restore
- Version pinning support for critical control-plane components
